name: Ashe Juniper

facts.how: A few as a juniper spice
facts.where: Hill Country slopes, the 'cedar' of Central Texas

caution: Seasoning only, and just a few berries; concentrated juniper is unsafe in quantity and in pregnancy. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: The shaggy-barked 'mountain cedar' that famously fills Central Texas air with pollen. Its blue berries are the useful part.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: Use a crushed berry or two to lend a resinous, gin-like note to hearty dishes.
